title: Al-Baqi, the Everlasting
tomorrow: Dadi wants to give it all away now. should she wait?

cards: Moving sales run on strange math. The couch goes for almost nothing, the lamp for free, and the thing that cost the most leaves first. Here is a stranger sum, from a hadith.
A sheep was slaughtered in the Prophet's household, peace be upon him, and the meat was given away. He asked what was left. Aisha said only the shoulder remained.
And he answered: all of it remains, except its shoulder. The part they kept was the part that was gone.

teach.b: To solve it, start with the Name. Al-Baqi, the Everlasting, the One who remains. The Qur'an puts it plainly in Surah al-Qasas: "Everything will perish save His countenance."
Phones, houses, mountains, the people we love. Everything has an ending except Him.
Now the second key, from Surah an-Nahl, in Pickthall's words: "That which ye have wasteth away, and that which Allah hath remaineth." Two piles.
What you hold runs out: the shoulder gets eaten, the dishes chip, the couch sags.

teach.h: GIVEN = WITH THE ONE WHO STAYS.
teach.b: What is with Allah stays, because He stays. So the riddle opens. Meat given as sadaqa, charity, has moved from the first pile to the second.
It's with the One who remains, so it remains. The shoulder they kept for dinner was simply dinner. Here's the thing to tell a friend tonight: in that hadith, the kitchen math runs backward.
What leaves your hands is what you keep. None of this makes owning things wrong; the family still ate the shoulder. It changes the grip.
If He remains, then the things that pass can be held loosely, enjoyed, and let go.

how: Muslims give sadaqa, voluntary charity, alongside the required zakat; the hadith of the sheep is often told to explain why what is given is what lasts.

o: the Everlasting, who remains when all else passes
the Patient, who waits before He answers you
the Keeper, who stores up what people own

games.q: solve the riddle — tap the pairs.

s: Al-Baqi just means Allah lasts longer than other things
it's not a longer lifespan: everything will perish save His countenance.
in the hadith, the part that 'remains' is the part given away
all of it remains, except its shoulder: the shoulder was the part they kept.

games.q: your little brother's sandcastle just washed away and he's sobbing. what does Al-Baqi let you tell him?
o: everything made passes; only He remains, so we can make things lightly.
build it farther up the beach; strong enough, it can last for good.
that's why making things is pointless; the sea always wins anyway.
games.why: Al-Baqi doesn't make things pointless. if He alone remains, the sandcastle can be loved, enjoyed, and let go.

practice: Put something small that you like in your open palm: a ring, a key, a pen. Rest your hand on your knee, palm up, fingers relaxed, and don't close them around it for the whole sit. Let it be held without being gripped.

wordCard.voice: Al-Baqi. The Everlasting, who remains when everything else has passed.

orig.note: Arabic: the Everlasting, the One who remains; from the traditional list of the Names.

carryVoice: Keep this close: he remains, and so does whatever you've given into his hands. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 2470 (the sheep: 'all of it remains except its shoulder')

sources.q: Everything will perish save His countenance.
That which ye have wasteth away, and that which Allah hath remaineth.
